title: inovex's demo is a Kubernetes-native Switchboard reference architecture its consultants reuse per engagement
content:
The artefact proposed for inovex is not a client integration but a reference architecture: Switchboard deployed the Kubernetes-native way, packaged so the firm's consultants can lift it into successive engagements. The unit of value is reuse across projects, which matches how a consultancy of that size actually absorbs new technology.

The research attaches an explicit caution to it. At roughly 500 people the decision is a committee rather than a champion, so this is a partnership conversation and not an outbound one. A reference architecture is the right object to bring to that conversation precisely because it is something the partner can own and resell, rather than a favour asked of one engineer.

That also changes the success criterion relative to the small-partner demos elsewhere in the corpus. This one succeeds when inovex's delivery organisation adopts it as a standard — a slower and more political outcome than shipping a single adapter, and one that should be planned for as such.
